title: The Blank Pages Rise
passages:
Elizabeth steps out of the cold water, feeling the chill on her skin, and looks down at the chest. The blank pages, once flat, now tremble and lift, spilling like thin sheets of paper. Their edges glow faintly, as if awaiting a hand.  

On the first page a single line shivers: *“The room is a throat that drinks words.”* The letters form without her touch, each stroke traced by a slender finger that matches the curve of the Second writer’s bell‑jawed face. The ledger’s mouth yawns, swallowing the soft rustle of her breath. A new line sits at the top, dated by nothing, signed only by the bell.  

Behind her, the skiff leans against the chest, its oars frozen mid‑row. Fishermen’s whispers dissolve into mist, and the water recedes farther, exposing more wet paper. The flood has finally given way, yet a thin film of black ink clings to the walls. If the room can be emptied, it must first seal its throat; until then the paper will keep growing.
